issue.title: Cannot depickle SQL-based Translator on SQLAlchemy>=2

repository.name: id-translation
repository.description: Turn meaningless IDs into human-readable labels.

issue.body:
```python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/dev/git/id-translation/src/id_translation/_translator.py", line 581, in restore
    ans = pickle.load(f)  # noqa: S301
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/dev/git/id-translation/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/util/langhelpers.py", line 1636, in __new__
    raise TypeError(
TypeError: Can't replace canonical symbol for unpickled with new int value -4533261097786850201
```
Works for `sqlalchemy<2`.

body:
Hi,

This may be a bug. Does setting the env variable 'DISABLE_SQLALCHEMY_CEXT_RUNTIME' changes anything?

No id does not seem to change anything.

This seems like a bug

>  Does setting the env variable 'DISABLE_SQLALCHEMY_CEXT_RUNTIME' changes anything?

No, same error.
@CaselIT If you feel like working through the docker image above to get us a proper test case that would be helpful

oh ok. Understood what's happening. the issue is that Row seems to serialize a symbol, and symbol uses `hash(name)`, and of course hash is random.

If you set the env variable `PYTHONHASHSEED=42` (or any value) the error goes away

Here where it's used:
https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/15a9aad96232dd3353084453a8789dbd714c33b7/lib/sqlalchemy/engine/cursor.py#L899

somehow CursorResultMetaData is serialized along with Row
I don't think we actually need that. we could just serialize `...` (ellipsis) here or any other default python value

> Here where it's used:
> 
> https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/15a9aad96232dd3353084453a8789dbd714c33b7/lib/sqlalchemy/engine/cursor.py#L899
> 
> somehow CursorResultMetaData is serialized along with Row

also this serialization seems broken. It serializes a 4 tuple, but otherwise it expect a 7 tuple.

I feel like we should serialized cursor result metadata as something else, like `SimpleResultMetaData`
Most of its method will break in various ways if called on a de-serialized result

we have tests for serialized results and there are very specific behaviors that have been carefully tested for many years, see below.    I'm not really sure how this exception is being produced or why the test below is not illustrating the failure.

if you can get me an MCVE I can fix this

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/15a9aad96232dd3353084453a8789dbd714c33b7/test/sql/test_resultset.py#L423-L499

the issue here mike is that python `hash()` is not stable, since every time python process it has a different random state, unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is set to a specific value.

symbol does internally `hash(name)` to create its int value, so each time the interpreter starts `symbol('unpickled')` has a different int value, breaking the check and tripping the exception.

What I don't understand is by `CursorResultMetaData` serializes itself as a kind of broken state (loads as 4 tuple in key map, instead of 7 tuple as expected).
It seems to me it could just serialized as `SimpleResultMetaData`

> What I don't understand is by `CursorResultMetaData` serializes itself as a kind of broken state (loads as 4 tuple in key map, instead of 7 tuple as expected). It seems to me it could just serialized as `SimpleResultMetaData`

all of those broken states have specific exception raises which would be gone if we used `SimpleResultMetaData`

PYTHONHASHSEED should be random I think when using tox, but in any case, the below doesnt fail:

```
$ PYTHONHASHSEED=random pytest test/sql/test_resultset.py -k pickle
```

so I need that test to be improved to show what's failing.    the test here is the bug

like, `symbol()` itself, we have no need for `symbol()` anymore.   it was pickleable in 1.4 but I might have broken it here.  we dont need it.  but bigger bug, the test suite isn't reproducing the problem.

the test above fails all-right. You can't test it in a single run on python, you need to create a pickle, save it, then load it from another interpreter. Otherwise loading it in the pickle in the same interpreter leads to the same hash
oh, I see.   then that's the problem, OK

no, that's not the problem.

I dont see how symbol() uses hash() for pickling.  it has a ``__reduce__()`` method.   Can you please show me a simple example?
